name: Toxicofera
blurb: Iguanas, monitor lizards and snakes. Molecular data group them together; anatomy has traditionally suggested a different arrangement.

relationship.note: A long-standing conflict between molecular and morphological evidence.

competing.name: Toxicofera (molecular)
competing.summary: Iguanians, anguimorphs (including monitor lizards) and snakes form one group, nested well inside the lizards.

competing.name: Iguania at the base (morphological)
competing.summary: Iguanians are the sister group of all other squamates (Scleroglossa), as anatomical studies have long found.
